result.headline: Output ch[3] pegged at 1900 us from 55.637 s; roll tracking then collapsed, cause unknown
result.explanation: Yes, a control fault occurred: actuator output ch[3] froze at 1900 us from 55.637 s. Roll tracking failed right after. The data cannot say whether the output, the controller or the airframe caused it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[3]] was varying, then held 1900 from t=55.637 s to the end of the recording (14.568 s, 44 samples)
evidence.shows: ch[3] stopped following the controller and sits at 1900 us to the end of the recording.

evidence.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[4]] changed level for good at t=56.396 s: median 1502 before, 1380.5 after us (10.1x its variation before)
evidence.shows: ch[4] and ch[5] (identical pair) shifted for good just after ch[3] froze, which looks like the other channels reacting.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a9 t=54.513 s: vehicle.attitude[yaw] followed control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] worse for a sustained stretch (typical |error| 40.444 vs 5.474) (see line 87; strength 4.455)
evidence.shows: Yaw tracking also degrades from 54.513 s, around the time ch[3] froze.

checked.check: Sequence 36-58 s against a 10 s baseline
checked.result: Setpoints, throttle and attitude left baseline first (from 36.102 s). ch[3], ch[4] and ch[5] left baseline at 46.737 s, before the freeze, so no single earliest sign appears.
ch[3] went 1504 to 1900 us with spread 0 (frozen). Roll tracking error went 0.886 to 12.875 deg. Yaw error went 7.133 to 40.444 deg.

checked.check: Compare at 41.248 s (the SHIFT line says ch[3] moved here)
checked.result: ch[3] was about 1506 us at 41.248 s and 1496 us at 54.863 s. The 1900 level starts at 55.637 s, so the SHIFT line's 41.248 s time is not the real onset.
checked.about: Early onset of the ch[3] fault

checked.result: Yaw error went 0.224 to 4.366 deg while the yaw attitude stayed near -43.495 deg. Nothing froze, and the later yaw setpoints move through large angles.

checked.check: Relation between yaw setpoint and ch[3], 5.021 to 39.958 s
checked.result: Correlation -0.325 (-0.382 at a 1.016 s lag). ch[3] is weakly tied to yaw before the fault, so which loop it serves is not established.

effects.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[4]] changed level for good at t=56.396 s: median 1502 before, 1380.5 after us (10.1x its variation before)
effects.why: The ch[4] and ch[5] shift follows the ch[3] freeze, so it is probably the controller compensating.

effects.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[1]] at t=64.498 s: 1514 -> 1432 us (step -82, 20.5x its usual variation)
effects.why: Throttle-loop output moving after the fault, likely a consequence.

outcomes.label: ch[3] follows command on bench
outcomes.means: The output and servo work; the saturation was commanded in flight (controller windup or an estimator or setpoint problem).
outcomes.then: Request the flight controller's raw log (rate and saturation flags).

outcomes.label: ch[3] sticks or the servo binds
outcomes.means: The fault is in the output, servo or wiring.
outcomes.then: Inspect the harness and servo, then replace the failed part.

hypotheses.claim: ch[3] output or its servo or wiring froze at 1900 us.
hypotheses.because: Frozen with zero spread from 55.637 s; roll and yaw tracking collapsed right after (cc_9). Signal is a recorded output, not the servo itself.

hypotheses.claim: The controller drove ch[3] to its limit under large attitude commands.
hypotheses.because: Roll setpoint was near -44.235 deg and the yaw setpoint was sweeping widely around then, so saturation could be commanded (cc_9, cc_10). Not separable from h1 on this data.

hypotheses.claim: Yaw tracking error comes from setpoint or estimate behaviour, not the actuator.
hypotheses.because: Yaw error rose at 6.868 s with nothing frozen (cc_8). Yaw attitude reaches 393.993 deg, which suggests angle wrapping is part of the picture.

hypotheses.claim: Start-up low-voltage and sensor-health warnings point to a sensor or power problem.
hypotheses.because: Both warnings appear once at 0.548 s, are start-up only, and nothing later points back to them (cc_3).
